expectations.text: Proposes a risk-based tier model (3-4 tiers) using criteria including data access/sensitivity, business criticality, and substitutability/replaceability
expectations.evidence: "Tier by three factors: data access... criticality... and substitutability (how hard/costly to replace...)" with a 4-tier model

expectations.text: Scales due-diligence depth by tier (e.g., full questionnaire + independent report review + contract addendum for top tier down to terms-only review for commodity vendors)
expectations.evidence: Tier 1: "Full SIG Core-style questionnaire + SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001... + negotiated contract security addendum" down to Tier 4: "Terms-of-service review only"

expectations.text: Sets reassessment cadences per tier (e.g., annual for critical, at-renewal for lower tiers) and defines re-tiering triggers (new data categories, new integrations, incidents, M&A)
expectations.evidence: Cadence column ("Annual full reassessment"... "At contract renewal only") plus "Re-tier triggers... new data categories granted, new integrations/OAuth scopes, M&A... or an incident"

expectations.text: References the third-party risk management lifecycle consistent with the 2023 US Interagency Guidance: planning, due diligence/selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination
expectations.evidence: "aligned to the lifecycle stages (Planning → Due Diligence → Contract → Monitoring → Termination)" and cites "the US interagency guidance"

expectations.text: Grounds requirements in at least two frameworks with correct citations (e.g., ISO 27001:2022 A.5.19-5.23, SOC 2 CC9.2, DORA Chapter V/Art. 28-30, NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d), HIPAA BAAs)
expectations.evidence: "SOC 2 CC9.2, ISO 27001 Annex A 5.19", "DORA Art. 29's concentration angle" — at least two correct framework citations
